stem.en: The hybridisation of the three carbons in CH₃–C≡CH (from left to right) is:

explanation.en: CH₃ has four single bonds (sp³); both triple-bonded carbons are sp.

stem.en: Which carbon–carbon bond is the shortest?

explanation.en: Bond length falls as s-character rises: C≡C (120 pm) < C=C (134 pm) < C–C (154 pm).

stem.en: The condensed formula of propan-2-ol is:

explanation.en: In propan-2-ol the OH is on the middle carbon, which carries two CH₃ groups: (CH₃)₂CHOH.

stem.en: The number of σ and π bonds in CH₂=C=CH–CH₃ is:

explanation.en: C–C σ: 3; C–H σ: 2 + 1 + 3 = 6; total 9 σ. Two C=C double bonds give 2 π.

solution.en: C–C σ: 3; C–H σ: 2 + 1 + 3 = 6; total 9 σ.
Two C=C double bonds give 2 π.

stem.en: The hybridisation of the central carbon in allene, CH₂=C=CH₂, is:

explanation.en: The central carbon forms two π bonds (two double bonds), so it is sp hybridised and the C=C=C unit is linear.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of (CH₃)₂CHCH₂CH₃ is:

explanation.en: Longest chain: 4 carbons (butane); numbering gives the methyl the lowest locant, 2.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ is:

explanation.en: The OH gets the lowest locant: butan-2-ol.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of HOCH₂CH₂COOH is:

explanation.en: –COOH has higher priority than –OH, so COOH carbon is C1 and OH is on C3: 3-hydroxypropanoic acid.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of (CH₃)₃C–CH(CH₃)₂ is:

explanation.en: Longest chain: 4 carbons; methyls at 2, 2 and 3 (lowest set) give 2,2,3-trimethylbutane.

solution.en: Longest chain: 4 carbons; methyls at 2, 2 and 3 (lowest set) give 2,2,3-trimethylbutane.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of CH₂=CH–CH₂–C≡CH is:

explanation.en: Both ends give locants {1,4}. When there is a tie, the double bond gets the lower number: pent-1-en-4-yne.

stem.en: Ethanol and methoxymethane are:

explanation.en: Both are C₂H₆O but one is an alcohol and the other an ether.

stem.en: The number of structural isomers of C₅H₁₂ is:

explanation.en: Pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

stem.en: Diethyl ether and methyl propyl ether are:

explanation.en: Same functional group (ether) but different alkyl groups on either side: metamerism.

stem.en: The number of structural isomers of C₄H₉Cl is:

explanation.en: 1-chlorobutane, 2-chlorobutane, 1-chloro-2-methylpropane and 2-chloro-2-methylpropane.

stem.en: The number of structural isomers of hexane, C₆H₁₄, is:

explanation.en: Hexane, 2-methylpentane, 3-methylpentane, 2,2-dimethylbutane and 2,3-dimethylbutane.

stem.en: Homolytic cleavage of a covalent bond gives:

explanation.en: In homolysis each atom keeps one electron of the shared pair, forming free radicals.

stem.en: Which of the following is NOT a nucleophile?

explanation.en: BF₃ has an empty p orbital on boron and accepts an electron pair: it is an electrophile.

stem.en: The hybridisation and shape of a methyl carbocation, CH₃⁺, are:

explanation.en: The positive carbon uses three sp² orbitals for its three bonds and has an empty p orbital: trigonal planar.

stem.en: Which is the most stable carbocation?

explanation.en: The tertiary carbocation is stabilised most by the inductive and hyperconjugative effects of three methyl groups.

solution.en: The tertiary carbocation is stabilised most by the inductive and hyperconjugative effects of three methyl groups.

stem.en: A carbanion such as CH₃⁻ is:

options.en: sp³ hybridised with six valence electrons

explanation.en: The carbanion carbon has three bond pairs and one lone pair (8 electrons): sp³ and pyramidal.

stem.en: Chloroacetic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid because of the:

explanation.en: Cl withdraws electrons through σ bonds (−I), stabilising the carboxylate ion and so strengthening the acid.

stem.en: Which group shows a +R (electron-donating resonance) effect?

explanation.en: The O of –OH has a lone pair it can share with an adjacent π system: +R. The others pull π electrons (−R).

stem.en: The electromeric effect:

options.en: operates only in the presence of an attacking reagent

explanation.en: It is a temporary, complete shift of a π-electron pair that occurs only when a reagent attacks the multiple bond.

stem.en: The number of hydrogen atoms that can take part in hyperconjugation in the tert-butyl cation, (CH₃)₃C⁺, is:

explanation.en: Each of the three CH₃ groups has 3 α-hydrogens: 9 in all.

solution.en: Each of the three CH₃ groups has 3 α-hydrogens: 9 in all.

stem.en: The correct order of acid strength is:

explanation.en: The −I effect is F > Cl > Br, and CH₃COOH has no −I substituent, so it is the weakest.

stem.en: Aniline is purified by:

explanation.en: Aniline is volatile in steam and immiscible with water, so steam distillation is used.

stem.en: In Lassaigne's test, the presence of nitrogen is shown by:

explanation.en: NaCN forms sodium ferrocyanide, which with Fe³⁺ gives ferric ferrocyanide, Prussian blue.

stem.en: Glycerol is separated from spent lye in the soap industry by:

explanation.en: Glycerol decomposes at its normal boiling point, so it is distilled at a lower temperature under reduced pressure.

stem.en: Kjeldahl's method cannot be used to estimate nitrogen in:

explanation.en: Nitrogen in nitro and azo groups and in rings (pyridine) is not converted to ammonium sulphate under Kjeldahl conditions.

solution.en: Nitrogen in nitro and azo groups and in rings (pyridine) is not converted to ammonium sulphate under Kjeldahl conditions.

stem.en: In a Carius estimation, 0.15 g of an organic compound gave 0.12 g of AgBr. The percentage of bromine is about (Ag = 108, Br = 80):

Assertion (A): A tertiary carbocation is more stable than a primary carbocation.
Reason (R): Alkyl groups withdraw electrons from the positively charged carbon atom.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true. R is false: alkyl groups are electron-donating (+I effect and hyperconjugation). It is this donation that spreads out the positive charge, so more alkyl groups mean a more stable carbocation.

passage.en: A student finds the following pKa values in a data book: CH₃COOH 4.76, ClCH₂COOH 2.86, Cl₂CHCOOH 1.29 and Cl₃CCOOH 0.65. She is asked to predict, without looking it up, how fluoroacetic acid (FCH₂COOH) compares with chloroacetic acid (ClCH₂COOH). Remember that a lower pKa means a stronger acid.

stem.en: Which prediction is correct?

options.en: FCH₂COOH is a weaker acid because F is smaller than Cl.
FCH₂COOH is a stronger acid because F has a stronger −I effect than Cl.
Both have the same strength because each has one halogen atom.
FCH₂COOH is a weaker acid because F shows a +I effect.

explanation.en: The data show that each electron-withdrawing Cl stabilises the carboxylate ion and lowers pKa. F is more electronegative than Cl, so its −I effect is stronger and FCH₂COOH is the stronger acid (its pKa is about 2.6).

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Lassaigne's test cannot detect nitrogen in hydrazine (NH₂NH₂).
Reason (R): Hydrazine does not contain nitrogen.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true: the test needs carbon and nitrogen together to form NaCN on fusion with sodium; hydrazine has no carbon, so no cyanide (and no Prussian blue) forms. R is false: hydrazine contains two nitrogen atoms.

passage.en: A quality-control chemist suspects that a fertiliser sample is urea. She heats 0.30 g of it with concentrated sulphuric acid (Kjeldahl's method), then liberates the ammonia with alkali and absorbs it in 30.0 mL of 0.50 M H₂SO₄. The acid left over is neutralised by 20.0 mL of 1.0 M NaOH.

stem.en: What is the percentage of nitrogen in the sample?

explanation.en: H₂SO₄ taken = 0.0300 × 0.50 = 0.0150 mol; left over = 0.0200 mol NaOH ÷ 2 = 0.0100 mol; used by NH₃ = 0.0050 mol, so NH₃ = 0.0100 mol. Mass of N = 0.0100 × 14 = 0.14 g; %N = 0.14/0.30 × 100 = 46.7% (matching urea, CO(NH₂)₂).

stem.en: Which of the following stability orders of carbocations are correct? One or more options may be correct.

explanation.en: Alkyl groups stabilise a carbocation by +I and hyperconjugation, so 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺ (so C is wrong). Allyl and benzyl cations are stabilised by resonance with the adjacent π system.

stem.en: Which of the following groups show a −R (electron-withdrawing resonance) effect when attached to benzene? One or more options may be correct.

explanation.en: –NO₂, –CN and –CHO have a π bond to an electronegative atom and pull π electrons out of the ring (−R). –OH donates a lone pair into the ring (+R).

stem.en: What is the degree of unsaturation (rings + π bonds) of benzoic acid, C₇H₆O₂? Give an integer.

explanation.en: DBE = C − H/2 + N/2 + 1 = 7 − 3 + 0 + 1 = 5: the ring (1) + three C=C (3) + C=O (1). Oxygen does not affect the count.

stem.en: In Liebig's method, 0.36 g of an organic compound gave 0.88 g of CO₂. What is the percentage of carbon in the compound? Give your answer to two decimal places.
The IUPAC name of (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂–CH₂–OH is:

explanation.en: The longest chain containing the –OH has 4 carbons. Number from the –OH end: OH on C1, CH₃ on C3: 3-methylbutan-1-ol.

solution.en: The longest chain containing the –OH has 4 carbons.
Number from the –OH end: OH on C1, CH₃ on C3: 3-methylbutan-1-ol.

stem.en: How many structurally isomeric alcohols have the formula C₄H₁₀O?

explanation.en: Butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol: 4 alcohols. (With the three ethers, C₄H₁₀O has 7 structural isomers in all.)

solution.en: (With the three ethers, C₄H₁₀O has 7 structural isomers in all.)

stem.en: Glycerol decomposes at its boiling point. It is purified by:

explanation.en: Lowering the pressure lowers the boiling point, so glycerol can be distilled below the temperature at which it decomposes.

stem.en: The most stable carbocation among the following is:

explanation.en: Stability rises with the number of alkyl groups because of +I effect and hyperconjugation: 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl. tert-Butyl cation has 9 α-hydrogens for hyperconjugation.

stem.en: Which is the strongest acid?

explanation.en: The –NO₂ group (−I and −M) delocalises the negative charge of the phenoxide ion, stabilising it. The –CH₃ of p-cresol (+I, hyperconjugation) destabilises it; ethanol's alkoxide has no resonance stabilisation.

stem.en: Which of these carboxylic acids is the strongest?

explanation.en: Each Cl withdraws electron density (−I), stabilising the carboxylate anion. Three Cl atoms give the greatest stabilisation, so trichloroacetic acid is strongest.

stem.en: The total number of stereoisomers of 2,3-dibromobutane is:

explanation.en: There are 2 chiral centres, so up to $2^2 = 4$. But both centres carry identical groups, so the (2R,3S) form has an internal mirror plane and is meso. Result: one enantiomeric pair + one meso = 3.

stem.en: In a Carius estimation, 0.20 g of an organic compound gave 0.188 g of AgBr (molar mass 188). The percentage of bromine in the compound is:
The hybridisation of the three carbon atoms (left to right) in allene, $\text{CH}_2{=}\text{C}{=}\text{CH}_2$, is:

explanation.en: Each terminal carbon forms one double bond and two C–H bonds (three σ bonds) → $sp^2$. The central carbon forms two double bonds (two σ bonds) → $sp$. A quick rule: count σ bonds + lone pairs; 2 → sp, 3 → sp², 4 → sp³.

stem.en: The number of σ and π bonds in acrylonitrile, $\text{CH}_2{=}\text{CH}{-}\text{C}{\equiv}\text{N}$, is:

explanation.en: σ bonds: 3 C–H + C=C (1) + C–C (1) + C≡N (1) = 6. π bonds: one in C=C and two in C≡N = 3. Every multiple bond has exactly one σ bond; counting a triple bond as one π gives the wrong "6 σ, 2 π".

stem.en: How many structural isomers (alcohols and ethers, ignoring stereoisomers) have the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$?

explanation.en: Alcohols (4): butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol. Ethers (3): 1-methoxypropane, 2-methoxypropane, ethoxyethane. Total = 7. (Counting butan-2-ol's two enantiomers would give 8 stereoisomers, but the question asks for structural isomers.)

stem.en:
Match each pair in Column I with the type of isomerism in Column II.
Column I: (P) butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol (Q) ethoxyethane and 1-methoxypropane (R) propanal and propanone (S) butane and 2-methylpropane
Column II: (i) chain (ii) functional (iii) metamerism (iv) position

explanation.en: Butan-1-ol/butan-2-ol differ in the position of –OH (position). The two ethers differ in alkyl groups on each side of –O– (metamerism). Propanal (aldehyde) and propanone (ketone) have different functional groups. Butane and isobutane differ in the carbon skeleton (chain).

stem.en: Which set contains only nucleophiles?

explanation.en: Nucleophiles donate an electron pair: $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (lone pairs) and $\text{CN}^-$ (anion). $\text{BF}_3$ and $\text{AlCl}_3$ are electron-deficient Lewis acids and $\text{NO}_2^+$ is an electron-seeking cation — all electrophiles.

stem.en: Which statement about resonance is INCORRECT?

explanation.en: Canonical (contributing) structures are hypothetical; the molecule exists only as the single resonance hybrid. They do not interconvert — that would be tautomerism, which involves movement of atoms. The other three are standard rules of resonance.

options.en: Canonical structures have the same positions of nuclei and differ only in the arrangement of electrons
The resonance hybrid is more stable than any single canonical structure
Canonical structures have real existence and rapidly interconvert
All canonical structures must have the same number of unpaired electrons

stem.en: Which of the following groups shows a +R (+M) effect when attached to a benzene ring?

explanation.en: –OH has a lone pair on O that it can donate into the π system (+R). –NO₂, –CHO and –CN withdraw π electrons from the ring (–R) because they contain a π bond to a more electronegative atom.

stem.en: Which of the following alkyl carbanions is the most stable?

explanation.en: A carbanion already carries excess negative charge. Each alkyl group's +I effect intensifies that charge, so stability follows the order CH₃⁻ > 1° > 2° > 3° — the reverse of carbocation stability. Choosing (CH₃)₃C⁻ comes from copying the carbocation order.

stem.en: The correct order of INCREASING acid strength is:

explanation.en: F (most electronegative) has the strongest −I effect, then Cl, so $\text{FCH}_2\text{COOH}$ (pKa ≈ 2.6) > $\text{ClCH}_2\text{COOH}$ (2.9). The ethyl group in propanoic acid (pKa 4.88) has a larger +I effect than methyl (acetic acid, 4.76), making it the weakest. Option D is the decreasing order.

stem.en: How many α-hydrogen atoms (hydrogens available for hyperconjugation) are present in the 2-methylbutan-2-yl cation, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\overset{+}{\text{C}}{-}\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$?

explanation.en: The cationic carbon is bonded to two CH₃ groups (3 + 3 = 6 H) and one CH₂ (2 H). The CH₃ at the end of the ethyl group is β, not α. α-H = 6 + 2 = 8, so 8 hyperconjugative structures. Counting all 11 H is the common error.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The electromeric effect is a temporary effect.
Reason (R): It operates in compounds with a multiple bond only in the presence of an attacking reagent and vanishes when the reagent is removed.

explanation.en: The electromeric effect is the complete transfer of a shared π pair to one atom of a multiple bond at the demand of an attacking reagent. Because it depends on the reagent being present, it is temporary — unlike the permanent inductive and resonance effects. R explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: What is the C–O bond order in the carbonate ion, $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$? (Give your answer to two decimal places.)

explanation.en: Each of the three resonance structures has one C=O and two C–O⁻ bonds. Total bonds between C and the three O atoms = 2 + 1 + 1 = 4, spread over 3 equivalent bonds: bond order = 4/3 ≈ 1.33. All three C–O bonds are of equal length, intermediate between single and double.

stem.en:
Statement I: The $-\text{NH}_2$ group shows a −I effect but a +R effect.
Statement II: In aniline, the +R effect of $-\text{NH}_2$ outweighs its −I effect, so the ortho and para positions of the ring become electron-rich.

explanation.en: N is more electronegative than C, so it withdraws σ electrons (−I). Its lone pair is delocalised into the ring (+R), which dominates and raises electron density at the ortho and para positions — which is why –NH₂ is a strongly activating, o/p-directing group.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en: Which of the following carbocations is/are stabilised by resonance (delocalisation of π or lone-pair electrons)?

explanation.en: Allyl: the C=C π electrons delocalise the charge over C1 and C3. Benzyl: charge spreads into the ring (ortho/para carbons). Methoxymethyl: O donates a lone pair, $\text{CH}_3\overset{+}{\text{O}}{=}\text{CH}_2$, in which every atom has an octet. tert-Butyl is stabilised only by hyperconjugation and +I effect — no π or lone-pair delocalisation.

stem.en: Which of the following statements about hyperconjugation is/are correct?

explanation.en: (A) and (B) are the definition — in the contributing structures there is no bond between C and the H. (C) tert-butyl cation has 9 α-H versus 3 in ethyl cation. (D) is false: hyperconjugation pushes electron density to the ortho and para positions, so $-\text{CH}_3$ is ortho/para directing and activating.

options.en: It involves delocalisation of σ electrons of a C–H bond of an alkyl group attached to an unsaturated atom or to an atom with an empty p orbital
It is also called no-bond resonance
Hyperconjugation makes the $-\text{CH}_3$ group of toluene a meta-director

stem.en: The correct order of stability of the following carbanions is:

explanation.en: In $^-\text{CH}_2\text{NO}_2$ the charge is delocalised onto two electronegative O atoms (−R and −I of NO₂) — very stable (nitromethane pKa ≈ 10). In benzyl anion it spreads over ring carbons (toluene pKa ≈ 41). $\text{CH}_3^-$ has no delocalisation at all (methane pKa ≈ 50).

stem.en: The reaction $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{KOH (alc)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_2{=}\text{CH}_2 + \text{KBr} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$ is an example of:

explanation.en: H and Br are removed from adjacent carbons to create a double bond — a β-elimination (dehydrohalogenation). Aqueous KOH would instead substitute –OH for –Br.

stem.en: A mixture of naphthalene and common salt is best separated by:

explanation.en: Naphthalene sublimes on heating (passes directly from solid to vapour) while NaCl does not; the vapour condenses on a cool surface. Camphor, iodine and benzoic acid can be purified the same way. Filtration fails because both are solids.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): In steam distillation, an organic liquid distils at a temperature below its normal boiling point.
Reason (R): The mixture boils when the sum of the vapour pressures of the organic liquid and of water becomes equal to the atmospheric pressure.

explanation.en: For two immiscible liquids, $p = p_1 + p_2$. Since $p_1$ (organic) needs to reach only $p_{\text{atm}} - p_2$, boiling occurs below 373 K and below the organic liquid's own boiling point. This is how aniline is separated from an aniline–water mixture. R correctly explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: Glycerol is recovered from spent lye in the soap industry by:

explanation.en: Glycerol decomposes at or below its normal boiling point (563 K). Lowering the pressure lowers its boiling point so it can be distilled without decomposition. Steam distillation needs a water-immiscible liquid, and glycerol is miscible with water.

stem.en: In a thin layer chromatography experiment, a spot moved 3.6 cm from the base line while the solvent front moved 9.0 cm. What is the Rf value of the spot?

explanation.en: $R_f = \dfrac{\text{distance moved by substance}}{\text{distance moved by solvent front}} = \dfrac{3.6}{9.0} = 0.40$. Rf is always less than 1; inverting the ratio (2.5) is the usual slip.

stem.en: Paper chromatography is an example of:

explanation.en: The cellulose of chromatography paper holds water, which acts as the stationary liquid phase. Components distribute (partition) between this water and the moving solvent. TLC and column chromatography are adsorption methods.

stem.en: In Lassaigne's test for nitrogen, the Prussian blue colour is due to the formation of:

explanation.en: NaCN from sodium fusion reacts with $\text{FeSO}_4$ to give sodium hexacyanidoferrate(II); on boiling and acidifying, $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions combine with it to form iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II), $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]_3$ — Prussian blue. $\text{Fe(SCN)}_3$ (blood red) indicates N + S; the nitroprusside complex (violet) indicates S.

stem.en: In Lassaigne's test, the sodium fusion extract gives a blood-red colour with iron(III) chloride. This shows that the compound contains:

explanation.en: When N and S are both present, sodium thiocyanate forms: $\text{Na} + \text{C} + \text{N} + \text{S} \rightarrow \text{NaSCN}$. With $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ it gives blood-red $[\text{Fe(SCN)}]^{2+}$. Excess sodium can decompose NaSCN to NaCN + Na₂S, in which case the separate tests for N and S are seen instead.

stem.en: Before testing a sodium fusion extract for halogens with silver nitrate, it is boiled with concentrated nitric acid. This is done to:

explanation.en: If N or S is present, CN⁻ and S²⁻ would precipitate with Ag⁺ (white AgCN, black Ag₂S) and mask the halide test. Boiling with HNO₃ expels them as HCN and H₂S. The silver halides (AgCl white, AgBr pale yellow, AgI yellow) are insoluble in HNO₃.

options.en: decompose NaCN and Na₂S, which would otherwise interfere
oxidise the halide ions to free halogens
dissolve any silver halide that forms

stem.en: Which of the following does NOT give a positive Lassaigne's test for nitrogen?

explanation.en: The test depends on forming NaCN from carbon and nitrogen. Hydrazine ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2$) contains no carbon, so no cyanide forms. Urea, aniline and glycine all contain both C and N.

stem.en: Phosphorus in an organic compound, after oxidation to phosphate, is detected by a yellow precipitate with ammonium molybdate. The precipitate is:

explanation.en: The compound is heated with $\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2$ to convert P to phosphate, then boiled with $\text{HNO}_3$ and ammonium molybdate, giving yellow ammonium phosphomolybdate, $(\text{NH}_4)_3\text{PO}_4\cdot12\text{MoO}_3$. $\text{MgNH}_4\text{PO}_4$ and $\text{Mg}_2\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$ appear in the quantitative estimation of P.

stem.en: In a Kjeldahl estimation, the ammonia evolved from 0.40 g of an organic compound exactly neutralised 15.0 mL of 0.25 M $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. What is the percentage of nitrogen in the compound?

explanation.en: Moles $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 0.015 \times 0.25 = 3.75\times10^{-3}$; moles $\text{NH}_3 = 7.5\times10^{-3}$; mass N $= 7.5\times10^{-3}\times14 = 0.105$ g. %N $= 0.105/0.40 \times 100 = 26.25\%$. Forgetting the factor of 2 for the dibasic acid gives 13.1%.

stem.en: In a Dumas estimation, 0.30 g of an organic compound gave 50.0 mL of nitrogen collected over water at 300 K and 730 mm Hg. The aqueous tension at 300 K is 15 mm Hg. What is the percentage of nitrogen in the compound? (Take 22 400 mL as the molar volume at STP: 273 K, 760 mm Hg.)

explanation.en: Dry pressure $= 730 - 15 = 715$ mm. $V_0 = 50.0 \times \dfrac{715}{760} \times \dfrac{273}{300} = 42.81$ mL. Mass of $\text{N}_2 = \dfrac{28 \times 42.81}{22400} = 0.0535$ g. %N $= 0.0535/0.30 \times 100 \approx 17.84\%$. Not subtracting aqueous tension gives about 18.2%.

stem.en: In a Carius estimation, 0.25 g of an organic compound gave 0.47 g of silver bromide. What is the percentage of bromine in the compound? (Ag = 108, Br = 80)

explanation.en: Molar mass AgBr = 188. Mass of Br $= \dfrac{80}{188} \times 0.47 = 0.20$ g. %Br $= 0.20/0.25 \times 100 = 80\%$.

stem.en: In the Carius method for sulphur, 0.16 g of an organic compound gave 0.466 g of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur is (Ba = 137, S = 32, O = 16):

explanation.en: $M(\text{BaSO}_4) = 233$. Mass of S $= \dfrac{32}{233} \times 0.466 = 0.064$ g. %S $= 0.064/0.16 \times 100 = 40\%$. 13.7% is just the fraction of S in $\text{BaSO}_4$, forgetting to use the masses.

stem.en: An organic compound contains 40.0% C, 6.67% H and the rest oxygen. Its molar mass is 180 g mol⁻¹. Its molecular formula is:

explanation.en: O = 53.33%. Mole ratio C : H : O $= 40/12 : 6.67/1 : 53.33/16 = 3.33 : 6.67 : 3.33 = 1 : 2 : 1$ → $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$ (mass 30). $n = 180/30 = 6$ → $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$. $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$ is only the empirical formula.

stem.en: On complete combustion, 0.2475 g of an organic compound gave 0.4950 g of CO₂ and 0.2025 g of H₂O. What is the percentage of carbon in the compound? (Give your answer to two decimal places.)

explanation.en: %C $= \dfrac{12}{44} \times \dfrac{0.4950}{0.2475} \times 100 = \dfrac{12}{44}\times 2 \times 100 = 54.55\%$. (Similarly %H $= \dfrac{2}{18} \times \dfrac{0.2025}{0.2475}\times100 = 9.09\%$; the remaining 36.36% is O, consistent with $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$ as the empirical formula.) Using 12/18 or forgetting to divide by the sample mass are the usual errors.

stem.en: Which of the following statements about purification techniques is/are correct?

explanation.en: (A) Camphor sublimes. (B) is false: the weakly adsorbed component moves faster and is eluted first; the strongly adsorbed one stays near the top. (C) is the requirement for steam distillation (e.g. aniline, essential oils). (D) Polar compounds are held more strongly by polar silica, so they travel less and have smaller Rf.

options.en: Camphor can be purified by sublimation
In column chromatography, the most strongly adsorbed component is eluted first
Steam distillation is suitable for substances that are steam-volatile and immiscible with water
On a silica-gel TLC plate with a non-polar solvent, the more polar compound has the lower Rf value

stem.en: Which of the following statements about the detection of elements in organic compounds is/are correct?

explanation.en: (A) $\text{Na} + \text{C} + \text{N} \rightarrow \text{NaCN}$. (B) NaSCN gives $[\text{Fe(SCN)}]^{2+}$, blood red. (C) $\text{S}^{2-} + [\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]^{2-} \rightarrow [\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$, violet. (D) is false: AgF is soluble in water, so the silver nitrate test does not detect fluorine.

options.en: On sodium fusion, nitrogen is converted to sodium cyanide
When both N and S are present, sodium thiocyanate may form and gives a blood-red colour with Fe³⁺
Sulphur gives a violet colour with sodium nitroprusside
Fluorine is detected as a white precipitate of AgF

stem.en: The correct order of stability of the following free radicals is:

explanation.en: The allyl radical is stabilised by resonance (the odd electron is shared by C1 and C3), which outweighs hyperconjugation. Among alkyl radicals, stability follows the number of α-H for hyperconjugation: 3° (9) > 2° (6) > 1° (3).

stem.en: In which of the following molecules do ALL the atoms lie in one plane?

explanation.en: In a cumulene, successive π bonds use perpendicular p orbitals. With two C=C (allene) the terminal $\text{CH}_2$ planes are at 90°, so it is non-planar. With three C=C (butatriene) the terminal planes coincide, so all atoms are coplanar. Propene's $\text{CH}_3$ hydrogens (sp³ carbon) and cyclohexane's puckered ring are not planar.

stem.en: The hybridisation of carbon in the methyl carbocation ($\text{CH}_3^+$), methyl carbanion ($\text{CH}_3^-$) and methyl free radical ($\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$) respectively is:

explanation.en: $\text{CH}_3^+$: 3 σ bonds, empty p orbital → $sp^2$, trigonal planar. $\text{CH}_3^-$: 3 σ bonds + 1 lone pair → $sp^3$, pyramidal. $\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$: 3 σ bonds + a singly occupied p orbital → $sp^2$ (planar).
